newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish interest rates to remain low - Bank of Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Irish interest rates to remain low - Bank of Ireland.

text.p: Irish interest rates are set to remain low despite strong growth in the Irish economy, buoyant credit conditions and a significant and ongoing depreciation of the Irish pound against sterling, Bank of Ireland Group Treasury said on Friday.

"Any decision to independently tighten interest rates would send out all the wrong signals about Ireland's EMU credentials and put further upward pressure on the currency within the ERM grid," the bank said in a research note.
"With German interest rates set to remain low over the coming year, any upward pressure on Irish rates is likely to be limited," it added.
Bank of Ireland said prospects for the Irish economy remained very good for 1997 against a background of low interest rates and a very generous fiscal stance.
It expects real GNP growth to reach 5.5 percent.
